title: Scientific Discoveries
tagline: Milestones that changed how we see the world.
source: Generated from “Timeline of scientific discoveries” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Egyptian numerals
events.text: The first deciphered numeral system is that of the Egyptian numerals, a sign-value system (as opposed to a place-value system).

events.title: Grammar
events.text: Grammar is first studied in India (note that Sanskrit Vyākaraṇa predates Pāṇini).

events.title: Archimedes
events.text: 3rd century BC: Archimedes discovers the sum/difference identity for trigonometric functions in the form of the "Theorem of Broken Chords".

events.title: Menaechmus
events.text: 4th century BC: Menaechmus discovers conic sections.

events.title: Aristarchus of Samos
events.text: Aristarchus of Samos proposes a basic heliocentric model of the universe.

events.title: Galen
events.text: 2nd century: Galen studies the anatomy of pigs.

events.title: Aryabhata
events.text: By 499: Aryabhata's work shows the use of the modern fraction notation, known as bhinnarasi.thumb|right|alt=Fragment of papyrus with clear Greek script, lower-right corner suggests a tiny zero with a double-headed arrow shape above it|Example of the

events.title: Varahamira
events.text: 6th century: Varahamira in the Gupta empire is the first to describe comets as astronomical phenomena, and as periodic in nature.

events.title: Virasena
events.text: Jain mathematician Virasena describes the integer logarithm.

events.title: Parameshvara
events.text: 15th century: Parameshvara discovers a formula for the circumradius of a quadrilateral.

events.title: Duns Scotus
events.text: Scottish priest Duns Scotus writes about the mutual beneficence of trade.

events.title: optical telescope
events.text: Earliest record of an optical telescope.

events.title: Francesco Redi
events.text: Francesco Redi: disproved idea of spontaneous generation.

events.title: Immanuel Kant
events.text: Immanuel Kant: Gaseous Hypothesis in Universal Natural History and Theory of Heaven.

references.label: Universal Natural History and Theory of Heaven

events.title: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
events.text: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck: teleological evolution.

events.title: Anselme Payen
events.text: Anselme Payen isolates first enzyme, diastase.

events.title: Louis Pasteur
events.text: Louis Pasteur: Germ theory.

events.title: John Hopkinson
events.text: 1880s: John Hopkinson develops three-phase electrical supplies, mathematically proves how multiple AC dynamos can be connected in parallel, improves permanent magnets, and dynamo efficiency, by the addition of tungsten, and describes how temperature

events.title: Max Planck
events.text: Max Planck: explains the emission spectrum of a black body

events.title: Henry Moseley
events.text: Henry Moseley: defined atomic number

events.title: Paul Dirac
events.text: Paul Dirac: Dirac equation (quantum mechanics)

events.title: Oswald Avery
events.text: Oswald Avery proves that DNA is the genetic material of the chromosome

events.title: André Petermann
events.text: André Petermann, Murray Gell-Mann and George Zweig: postulates quarks, leading to the Standard Model

events.title: Mary-Claire King
events.text: Mary-Claire King discovers the link between heritable breast cancers and a gene found on chromosome 17q21.

events.title: Andre Geim
events.text: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov isolated graphene, a monolayer of carbon atoms, and studied its quantum electrical properties.

events.title: human genome
events.text: The standard reference gene, GRCh38.p14, of the human genome, is fully sequenced and contains 3.1 billion base pairs.
